newsitem.title: CANADA: Goodale denies Canada willing to curb grain export.
newsitem.headline: Goodale denies Canada willing to curb grain export.

text.p: Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale denied on Thursday that Canada was willing to limit grain exports to the United States.

"It's absolutely false," he said in reaction to testimony before Congress in which a U.S. official said Washington understood Canada would try not to exceed 1.4 to 1.5 million tonnes of wheat and barley exports to the United States .

"Quite frankly I'm not quite sure what part of the word 'No' these people continue to fail to understand, but there is no cap, no limit, no agreement and absolutely no inclination on the part of Canada for anything in that direction."
The remarks before a U.S. House agriculture subcommittee were made by August Schumacher, head of the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Foreign Agriculture Service.
Schumacher added: "This administration simply will not tolerate market disruptions by Canadian grain."

Goodale said in an interview: "I presume there is in some of that some playing to the local audience in the United States, but quite frankly it's so erroneous and factually wrong that it borders on the mischievous.
"There is no cap and there's no limit."
Asked if there might be a cap in the future, he said: "Canada is not going to engage in that kind of mug's game. It's just totally self-defeating.
"The facts are our grain is fairly traded. We are fully within all of the rules of the NAFTA (North American Free Trade Agreement) and the WTO (World Trade Organization).

"The United States has itself over the last number of years investigated Canadian trade flows in grain on at least three separate occasions. On every one of those occasions the Canadian record has been vindicated. There is just nothing to support this kind of allegation or this kind of demand."

Goodale said wheat exports to the United States in 1996-97 were up somewhat with the year before and more or less in line with 1994-95, the year when Canada had agreed to cap its wheat exports at 1.5 million tonnes, but nowhere near the all-time record figures from 1993-94.

"If you go back to '94-'95, you'll find that that arithmetic is very similar to this year's arithmetic," he said, elaborating that when the 1996-97 year was finished the exports was likely to be in the same "ballpark" as 1994-95.

Goodale has said in the past that Canada was willing to sit down with the United States to clarify the record but not to entertain limits. Asked if Washington might be confusing this for a willingness to curb exports, he said:

"In the messages that have been conveyed to the United States officials, the language has been very precise, very direct, very clear and on occasion very colorful. The message could not have been mistaken."
